parent_channels.scene_or_process: A repeated summons gathers a worshipper who turns toward a fixed direction, performs the prayer's postures, recites an allotted office, and counts praise on beads.
parent_channels.active_motifs: repeated call to prayer (`quranic:root_000209:B004/m01`); fixed direction faced in prayer (`quranic:root_001198:B005/m01`); formal sequence of standing, bowing, and prostrating (`quranic:root_000879:B003/m01`); recurring allotted portion of prayer or recitation (`quranic:root_000315:B002/m02`); beads used to count praise (`quranic:root_000666:B006/m01`)
parent_channels.synthesis: The motifs form one repeatable rite: summons, orientation, bodily sequence, assigned recitation, and tangible count. This materializes what the later generation loses at 19:59. Neglected prayer is not an abstract attitude but the abandonment of a directed, embodied, and regularly measured office.

parent_channels.name: S11. Lead voice, answering singer, refrain, and drum
parent_channels.scene_or_process: A lead voice is answered by a following singer, a melodic line returns as a refrain, listeners attend, and a one-sided drum marks the performance.
parent_channels.active_motifs: answering voice that follows a singer (`quranic:root_000186:B007/m01`); paired exchange between performers (`quranic:root_000563:B008/m01`); raised voice in song, reading, or weeping (`quranic:root_001035:B009/m01`); melodic singing and softened recitation (`quranic:root_001110:B003/m01`); attentive enjoyment of a skilled voice (`quranic:root_000741:B007/m01`); returning refrain or vocal echo (`quranic:root_000544:B007/m01`); one-sided drum (`quranic:root_001281:B012/m01`)
parent_channels.synthesis: This is an antiphonal performance rather than a loose sound inventory: one voice leads, another follows, the line returns, an audience hears, and percussion supplies pulse. It reframes the Surah's chain of recitation and response as responsive acoustics, supporting the prophetic succession in which transmitted words move from one voice to another and culminate in bodily submission and tears at 19:58.

parent_channels.name: S12. Courtship message, marriage contract, and bridal escort
parent_channels.scene_or_process: Suitors contact a previously married woman, a public contract establishes the union, and the bride is escorted to a prepared canopy and household.
parent_channels.active_motifs: widowed or divorced woman receiving messages from suitors (`quranic:root_000563:B009/m01`); marriage contract and solemnization (`quranic:root_001444:B004/m01`); marriage represented as protection for the unmarried (`quranic:root_001110:B006/m01`); bride escorted to her husband (`quranic:root_001583:B006/m01`); bridal canopy and entry into married life (`quranic:root_000156:B006/m01`)
parent_channels.synthesis: The branches supply a socially legible sequence for household formation: approach by message, binding contract, escorted transfer, and entry beneath a prepared canopy. Its lexical presence usefully pressures Mary's accusation scene because her pregnancy bypasses this ordinary public sequence; the Surah locates legitimacy instead in divine message, decree, and the child's testimony.

parent_channels.name: S13. Lament, bier, shroud, and burial
parent_channels.scene_or_process: Mourners voice grief, the dead person is carried on a bier, wrapped, laid on the right side, hidden in a grave, and covered by a raised mound.
parent_channels.active_motifs: funeral tears and voiced grief (`quranic:root_000146:B001/m02`); formal wail over the dead (`quranic:root_001633:B009/m01`); bier or carrying frame (`quranic:root_000067:B008/m01`); shroud covering the body (`quranic:root_000266:B009/m01`); grave as a concealing enclosure (`quranic:root_000266:B009/m02`); corpse laid on its right side (`quranic:root_001698:B007/m01`); burial that removes the body from sight (`quranic:root_001117:B009/m01`); raised grave mound (`quranic:root_000223:B002/m02`)
parent_channels.synthesis: The motifs form a full mortuary transition from audible grief to complete visual concealment. Carrying, shrouding, right-side placement, interment, and mounding progressively remove the person from ordinary perception. This materializes the Surah's repeated death-and-raising formula and sharpens resurrection as the reversal of a deliberate burial process: the one hidden from every human sense is made to stand and arrive individually.

parent_channels.name: S14. Lot arrows dividing a slaughtered camel
parent_channels.scene_or_process: Players draw lot arrows from a leather holder, and the result assigns portions of a slaughtered camel.
parent_channels.active_motifs: leather holder collecting the lot arrows (`quranic:root_000532:B010/m01`); players casting or drawing lots (`quranic:root_001694:B007/m01`); camel slaughtered and divided according to the arrows (`quranic:root_001694:B007/m02`); named superior or winning lot-arrow (`quranic:root_001042:B009/m02`)
parent_channels.synthesis: This is a complete allocation practice: lots are stored together, drawn by players, ranked, and translated into shares of meat. The chance-governed division usefully pressures the Surah's language of decree, exact enumeration, and solitary arrival. Final allotment is not a lucky draw from a common case but a fully known judgment in which no individual or claim escapes account.

parent_channels.name: S15. Perfume ground, compounded, and carried on air
parent_channels.scene_or_process: Aromatic powder and camphor are crushed on a broad slab and in a mortar, compounded into an applied perfume, and perceived as scent moving on air.
parent_channels.active_motifs: aromatic powder (`quranic:root_000511:B003/m01`); broad perfume-grinding slab under the prayer root (`quranic:root_000879:B008/m01`); the same grinding-stone object under the fire root (`quranic:root_000880:B009/m01`); mortar or pounding tool (`quranic:root_001608:B004/m01`); camphor as perfume material (`quranic:root_001307:B011/m01`); compounded perfume applied as a coating (`quranic:root_000434:B010/m01`); fragrance perceived by smell (`quranic:root_000609:B004/m01`); breeze carrying the result (`quranic:root_000609:B003/m02`)
parent_channels.synthesis: The ingredients and tools form one perfumery operation, with the prayer and fire roots converging on the same grinding slab before the mixture becomes an invisible but perceptible fragrance. This materially reframes the Surah's hidden-to-manifest pattern: crushing and compounding remain unseen within the preparation, while their efficacy is disclosed as scent borne on the same lexical air whose root also names the spirit sent to Mary.

parent_channels.name: S16. P1 + P4 bridge - Naming as a test of equivalence
parent_channels.scene_or_process: A designation is assigned and then tested for a prior namesake or any possible peer capable of matching its bearer.
parent_channels.active_motifs: name as a public designation (`quranic:root_000745:B005/m01`); namesake or counterpart entitled to the same designation (`quranic:root_000745:B005/m02`); peer comparison that tests whether another can match the bearer (`quranic:root_000745:B007/m01`)
parent_channels.synthesis: The P1-P4 bridge is a contrast in the scope of equivalence. John's assigned name has no prior human namesake at 19:7; at 19:65 the same root asks whether any counterpart for God can be known at all. Human uniqueness is novelty within a created sequence, while divine uniqueness is absolute unmatchability.

parent_channels.name: S17. P1 + P4 bridge - Prior creation as precedent
parent_channels.scene_or_process: A completed act of creation is recalled and entered as precedent for judging whether a later act is possible.
parent_channels.active_motifs: origination and bringing a creature into existence (`quranic:root_000434:B002/m01`); a thing as an entity that can be known and spoken about (`quranic:root_000831:B001/m01`); retrieval of a prior fact from memory (`quranic:root_000516:B003/m01`)
parent_channels.ayah_anchors: 19:9 (خ ل ق, ش ي ء); 19:67 (ذ ك ر, خ ل ق, ش ي ء)
parent_channels.synthesis: The P1-P4 bridge is a repeated proof scene with a reversal of discourse role. At 19:9 prior creation reassures Zechariah that an impossible-seeming birth is easy; at 19:67 the same precedent rebuts the human denial of resurrection. The evidence does not change, but its force moves from consolation to cross-examination.

parent_channels.name: S18. P2 + P5 bridge - False filiation becoming material collapse
parent_channels.scene_or_process: A genealogical claim assigns a parent-offspring relation, fabricates what was not said, and triggers a cascading structural failure.
parent_channels.active_motifs: parents defined through actual birth (`quranic:root_001683:B002/m01`); something generated from another as its product (`quranic:root_001683:B005/m01`); false speech attributed to one who did not say it (`quranic:root_001272:B005/m01`); claim of lineage or offspring (`quranic:root_000478:B002/m01`); one part falling after another in a collapse (`quranic:root_000478:B005/m01`)
parent_channels.synthesis: The P2-P5 bridge is a causal reversal between true generative speech and fabricated genealogy. P2 identifies Jesus through Mary, servanthood, and a word of truth while denying divine offspring; P5 repeats the offspring attribution as false speech. The claim root also names successive collapse, so the falling cosmos materializes the consequence of assigning a parent-child relation where the Surah denies one.

parent_channels.name: S19. P3 -> P4 bridge - Succession as a relay that can fail
parent_channels.scene_or_process: One cohort follows another and occupies its place, but continuity of position can either transmit the prior practice or break before later renewal.
parent_channels.active_motifs: successor taking a predecessor's place or office (`quranic:root_000433:B001/m01`); cohorts alternating one after another (`quranic:root_000433:B006/m01`); bodily or ranked following behind a predecessor (`quranic:root_000186:B001/m01`); uninterrupted sequence of acts or occupants (`quranic:root_001684:B002/m01`); fresh growth returning after earlier vegetation has passed or dried (`quranic:root_000433:B010/m01`)
parent_channels.synthesis: The P3-P4 bridge is a role progression interrupted at the pericope boundary. P3 closes with a guided line receiving recitation; P4 opens with replacements who occupy the inherited position but abandon its prayer. Replacement therefore preserves office without guaranteeing practice, while the returning-growth sense gives repentance the form of renewed life after a failed season.

parent_channels.name: S20. P2 -> P5 bridge - Reversion from apparent owner to servant
parent_channels.scene_or_process: Claimed rights and holdings revert to their owner, while the apparent possessor returns in person and arrives under servant status.
parent_channels.active_motifs: return to a former source or state (`quranic:root_000544:B001/m01`); restoration of a right to its owner (`quranic:root_000609:B006/m01`); personal arrival at an appointed destination (`quranic:root_000009:B001/m01`); owned servant in contrast to a free possessor (`quranic:root_000973:B001/m01`)
parent_channels.synthesis: The P2-P5 bridge is a legal role reversal. P2 closes by declaring that the earth and its occupants revert to God and return to Him. P5 enacts that reversion: the claimant's supposed holdings are inherited away, he arrives without them, and all beings arrive as servants. Apparent possession is thus temporary custody that resolves into returned right and acknowledged ownership.

parent_channels.name: S21. P2 (19:16-40) - Vowed fasting as bodily and verbal restraint
parent_channels.scene_or_process: A vow makes abstention binding across bodily appetite and speech, so the person neither consumes nor answers.
parent_channels.active_motifs: self-imposed obligation to God (`quranic:root_001488:B002/m01`); fasting from food, drink, intimacy, and other prohibited acts (`quranic:root_000894:B001/m01`); fasting of the tongue through silence (`quranic:root_000894:B002/m01`)
parent_channels.synthesis: The two fasting senses make Mary's vow a coordinated discipline rather than generic quiet: bodily intake is restrained and the tongue is withheld under one assumed obligation. This supports the public-proof reading by transferring the necessary answer away from the accused mother; her abstention leaves the child to speak the vindicating testimony.

parent_channels.name: S22. Concealed-hand guessing from riddle to reveal
parent_channels.scene_or_process: Players conceal a quantity in the hand, pose an odd-or-even challenge in riddling form, and open the hand to disclose the answer.
parent_channels.active_motifs: game of revealing what is hidden in the hand (`quranic:root_000400:B010/m01`); masked challenge designed to elicit a hidden answer (`quranic:root_000478:B007/m01`); odd-or-even choice over what the fist contains (`quranic:root_000637:B005/m01`)
parent_channels.synthesis: This is a complete uncertainty-and-disclosure game: concealment creates a binary guess, the riddle solicits an answer, and opening the hand resolves it. It usefully pressures the final census at 19:94-95. Human players infer a hidden number by chance and reveal, whereas divine enumeration requires neither guessing nor disclosure and still distinguishes every individual exactly.

parent_channels.name: S23. P2 (19:16-40) - Sewing and seasoning a waterskin
parent_channels.scene_or_process: Hide sections are sewn into a water vessel, seasoned with clay and water until the seams seal, filled, and emptied through a controlled lower mouth.
parent_channels.active_motifs: stitching one hide edge to another (`quranic:root_000121:B006/m01`); leather waterskin used to draw water (`quranic:root_001212:B009/m01`); clay-and-water seasoning that improves taste and seals stitching (`quranic:root_000783:B013/m01`); filling a waterskin or vessel (`quranic:root_000905:B003/m01`); lower outlet through which the water pours (`quranic:root_001009:B006/m01`)
parent_channels.synthesis: The motifs form one commissioning process: separate skins become a container, porous stitching is swollen and sealed, the vessel is filled, and its contents leave only through the intended mouth. This materializes Mary's commanded drink and the Surah's protected-boundary reading. Successful concealment does not prevent provision from emerging; it preserves the contents for controlled release.

parent_channels.name: S24. P3 -> P4 bridge - Race order from leader to third
parent_channels.scene_or_process: Horses run toward a fixed finish, with a winner in front, a second horse tracking its hindquarters, and a third completing the ordered places.
parent_channels.active_motifs: horse running with extended forelegs (`quranic:root_000666:B004/m01`); leading racehorse (`quranic:root_000104:B008/m01`); winner reaching the finish (`quranic:root_001684:B012/m01`); second horse following with its head at the leader's rear (`quranic:root_000879:B006/m01`); horse arriving third (`quranic:root_000203:B003/m01`)
parent_channels.synthesis: The P3-P4 bridge is ordered pursuit. The lexical *musalli* is the second horse that stays immediately behind the leader, while a third horse and a finish line make succession measurable. This reframes the transition from the guided prophetic line to replacements who lose prayer at 19:59: neglecting *al-salat* resembles falling out of the close following position by which the course is carried forward.

parent_channels.name: S25. P2 (19:16-40) - Calf-induced letdown and hand milking
parent_channels.scene_or_process: A small amount of milk is retained in the udder, a calf is brought near to induce letdown and then removed, the udder is massaged, and fingertips draw a continuing flow.
parent_channels.active_motifs: retained milk that calls forth the rest (`quranic:root_000478:B003/m01`); borrowed calf used briefly to induce the dam's milk (`quranic:root_001355:B007/m01`); massaging the udder to start flow (`quranic:root_001416:B001/m01`); milking with the fingertips (`quranic:root_001165:B005/m01`); milk flowing in succession (`quranic:root_000563:B006/m01`)
parent_channels.synthesis: The scene is a precise release mechanism rather than a general dairy field. A retained portion, the young animal's presence, manual stimulation, and fingertip extraction successively turn stored nourishment into flow. It materializes the birth-and-provision reading by showing new life eliciting an ordered economy of care: provision is present, but relation and skilled action make it available.

parent_channels.name: S26. P5 (19:77-98) - Manumission through scheduled written payments
parent_channels.scene_or_process: An enslaved person and owner enter a written agreement, payments fall due in stages, and completed performance changes the person's legal status to freedom.
parent_channels.active_motifs: written manumission contract between owner and servant (`quranic:root_001283:B005/m01`); money divided into scheduled installments (`quranic:root_001283:B005/m02`); release produced by satisfying the written terms (`quranic:root_001283:B005/m03`)
parent_channels.synthesis: This branch supplies a full legal transformation inside the writing root: record, deferred performance, and release. It usefully pressures P5's conjunction of written liability and universal servanthood. Human bondage can be terminated by a payable document, but the record extended at 19:79 culminates in every being arriving as a servant at 19:93; that final relation is not a human status that money can discharge.

parent_channels.name: S27. P2 (19:16-40) - Midwife receiving child and afterbirth
parent_channels.scene_or_process: A birth attendant positions a receiving hand for the emerging child while membrane and fluid come out with or around the newborn.
parent_channels.active_motifs: midwife receiving the child into the hand at birth (`quranic:root_001198:B007/m01`); membrane, fluid, or placenta emerging with the child (`quranic:root_000373:B008/m01`)
parent_channels.synthesis: The motifs form an ordinary obstetric reception scene with a human receiver and the material that accompanies birth. Its activation usefully pressures Mary's solitary labor at 19:23: the expected receiving hand is absent, yet the bodily event is not abstracted away. Safe emergence without that attendant sharpens the role of the provision and care supplied around her.

parent_channels.name: S28. P2 + P5 bridge - Rocking motion reversing into demolition
parent_channels.scene_or_process: A caregiver applies small repeated movements until an infant settles into stable sleep; the same motion root later names a collapse that leaves no structure settled.
parent_channels.active_motifs: caregiver rocking a child to sleep (`quranic:root_001580:B006/m01`); stillness and stable persistence as the settling outcome (`quranic:root_000501:B001/m01`)
parent_channels.synthesis: The P2-P5 bridge is a reversal of scale and outcome. Bounded rocking stabilizes vulnerable infant life, while the *hadd* of 19:90 brings mountains down when false filiation convulses the cosmos. A motion associated with nurture is inverted into demolition, making the consequence of the offspring claim a material undoing of the Surah's birth-and-care scenes.

parent_channels.name: S29. P2 (19:16-40) - Withdrawal that refuses foundling abandonment
parent_channels.scene_or_process: A mother casts away a child for another person to find, but Mary's withdrawal with her child reverses that social scene through return and public carrying.
parent_channels.active_motifs: discarded child left to be taken up by someone else (`quranic:root_001466:B007/m01`)
parent_channels.synthesis: The foundling sense gives withdrawal a complete and dangerous alternative outcome: distance can become abandonment when a child is cast away for an unknown finder. Mary's repeated withdrawal activates that pressure but does not complete it. By carrying the child back to her people at 19:27, she turns concealment into temporary protection rather than an erasure of relation or responsibility.

word_analysis_qac_alignment.note: aligned_qac_word_ref does NOT resolve against qac_morphemes for this ayah: word-analysis counts orthographic words where QAC counts morphological words. Upstream defect in quran-data's word-analysis; deliberately not auto-repaired (renumbering would fabricate identities).
